subject: Information Theory
title: Metcalfe's Law
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Metcalfe's Law.

hook.text: A fax machine is useless alone. Two are useful. A million form a transformative network. Value grows with connections.

buildup.text: Metcalfe's law: a network's value is proportional to the square of its users. n users create n(n-1)/2 connections.

discovery.text: This explains why platforms push for growth. Each new user adds value to every existing user. Positive feedback.

twist.text: Metcalfe's law overestimates. Not all connections are equally valuable. Odlyzko proposed n·log(n) as more realistic.

climax.text: Network effects create winner-take-all markets. Once a platform leads, switching costs lock users in.

punchline.text: More users, more value. Networks reward scale.

quiz.question: What does Metcalfe's law claim about network value?
options: It grows proportionally to the square of the number of users
